answer: A microgrid on an ivory-colored knoll hires AI controllers to steady each pulse of electricity. Payment follows meter-signed net energy delivered through a sealed feeder during a randomly assigned dispatch window, not the number of controller names. The task nonce makes a replayed meter trace invalid. To profit through many identities, an attacker must install separate metered capacity and supply real energy, which costs equipment and fuel. A compromised meter or colluding grid operator could still fabricate delivery, so independent meters and surprise physical audits are necessary.
